3. **20% SL is far too wide for a liquidity hunt**: hunt trades are designed for a 5 min in-out, but 20% SL means the exchange will not close it until a huge move — they're meant to have ~1% SL tight to the stop level.

User: in your perspective am I being too agressive with 10x and 10% profit?

GitHub Copilot: Yes, that combo is aggressive for most conditions.

At 10x leverage:
1. A 10% TP on ROE is only about a 1% move in price.
2. That can look easy, but noise, spread, and slippage can hit you fast.
3. If your stop is tight (for example 5% ROE), you are risking about a 0.5% adverse move, which is common intrabar on alts.

1. Liquidity is strong.
2. Trend structure is clear.
3. You avoid chop/ranging periods.

A more durable baseline is:
1. 3x to 5x leverage for normal signals.
2. Keep 10x only for top-tier setups.
3. Use smaller size at higher leverage.
4. Require confirmation (which you already added with candle gating).

const fs=require('fs');
const data=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/Users/islam/dev/hype-trading/apps/api/hl-candles-90d-all.json','utf8'));

function sma(arr, n, i){ if(i-n+1<0) return null; let s=0; for(let k=i-n+1;k<=i;k++) s+=arr[k]; return s/n; }
function rsi(closes, period=14){
  const out=Array(closes.length).fill(null);
  let gain=0, loss=0;
  for(let i=1;i<=period;i++){
    const d=closes[i]-closes[i-1]; if(d>=0) gain+=d; else loss-=d;
  }
  let avgGain=gain/period, avgLoss=loss/period;
  out[period]=avgLoss===0?100:100-(100/(1+avgGain/avgLoss));
  for(let i=period+1;i<closes.length;i++){
    const d=closes[i]-closes[i-1];
    const g=d>0?d:0, l=d<0?-d:0;
    avgGain=(avgGain*(period-1)+g)/period;
    avgLoss=(avgLoss*(period-1)+l)/period;
    out[i]=avgLoss===0?100:100-(100/(1+avgGain/avgLoss));
  }
  return out;
}
function stochRsi(rsiVals, period=14, kS=3, dS=3){
  const srsi=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null), k=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null), d=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null);
  for(let i=0;i<rsiVals.length;i++){
    if(i-period+1<0||rsiVals[i]==null) continue;
    let min=Infinity,max=-Infinity,ok=true;
    for(let j=i-period+1;j<=i;j++){ const v=rsiVals[j]; if(v==null){ok=false;break;} if(v<min)min=v; if(v>max)max=v; }
    if(!ok) continue;
    srsi[i]=(max===min)?0.5:(rsiVals[i]-min)/(max-min);
    const kv=sma(srsi, kS, i); if(kv!=null) k[i]=kv*100;
    const dv=sma(k, dS, i); if(dv!=null) d[i]=dv;
  }
  return {srsi,k,d};
}

function analyze(sym){
  const rows=data[sym]?.['1d'];
  if(!rows||rows.length<40) return null;
  const close=rows.map(r=>+r.close), vol=rows.map(r=>+r.volume), high=rows.map(r=>+r.high), low=rows.map(r=>+r.low);
  const ret=close.map((c,i)=> i? (c/close[i-1]-1)*100 : null);
  const r=rsi(close,14); const s=stochRsi(r,14,3,3);

  const events=[];
  for(let i=25;i<rows.length;i++){
    const r1=ret[i]??0;
    const r2=((close[i]/close[i-2])-1)*100;
    const r3=((close[i]/close[i-3])-1)*100;
    const vma7=sma(vol,7,i-1); const volRatio=vma7?vol[i]/vma7:null;
    if((r1>=18 || r2>=25 || r3>=30) && (volRatio==null || volRatio>=1.4)) events.push(i);
  }

  const unique=[];
  for(const i of events){ if(!unique.length || i-unique[unique.length-1]>3) unique.push(i); }

  const rowsOut=[];
  for(const i of unique){
    const p=i-1;
    const vma7=sma(vol,7,p), vma14=sma(vol,14,p);
    const volRatio7=vma7?vol[p]/vma7:null;
    const volRatio14=vma14?vol[p]/vma14:null;

    const start=Math.max(0,p-20);
    let swingH=-Infinity,swingL=Infinity;
    for(let j=start;j<=p;j++){ if(high[j]>swingH)swingH=high[j]; if(low[j]<swingL)swingL=low[j]; }
    const range=swingH-swingL;
    let fibPos=null; // 0 near low, 1 near high
    if(range>0) fibPos=(close[p]-swingL)/range;

    rowsOut.push({
      date:new Date(rows[i].timestamp).toISOString().slice(0,10),
      pumpDayReturnPct:+(ret[i]??0).toFixed(2),
      pump3dReturnPct:+(((close[i]/close[Math.max(0,i-3)])-1)*100).toFixed(2),
      pre_rsi: r[p]==null?null:+r[p].toFixed(2),
      pre_stochK: s.k[p]==null?null:+s.k[p].toFixed(2),
      pre_stochD: s.d[p]==null?null:+s.d[p].toFixed(2),
      pre_stochCrossUp: (s.k[p]!=null&&s.d[p]!=null&&s.k[p]>s.d[p]&&s.k[p-1]!=null&&s.d[p-1]!=null&&s.k[p-1]<=s.d[p-1])||false,
      pre_volRatio7: volRatio7==null?null:+volRatio7.toFixed(2),
      pre_volRatio14: volRatio14==null?null:+volRatio14.toFixed(2),
      pre_fibPos_20d: fibPos==null?null:+fibPos.toFixed(2)
    });
  }
  return rowsOut;
}

for(const sym of ['BEAT','ALLO']){

  console.log('\n===',sym,'events',out?.length||0,'===');
  if(!out){console.log('no data');continue;}
  for(const r of out) console.log(JSON.stringify(r));
}

function rsi(closes, period=14){ const out=Array(closes.length).fill(null); let g=0,l=0; for(let i=1;i<=period;i++){const d=closes[i]-closes[i-1]; if(d>=0)g+=d; else l-=d;} let ag=g/period, al=l/period; out[period]=al===0?100:100-(100/(1+ag/al)); for(let i=period+1;i<closes.length;i++){const d=closes[i]-closes[i-1]; const gg=d>0?d:0, ll=d<0?-d:0; ag=(ag*(period-1)+gg)/period; al=(al*(period-1)+ll)/period; out[i]=al===0?100:100-(100/(1+ag/al)); } return out; }
function stochRsi(rsiVals, period=14, kS=3, dS=3){ const sr=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null), k=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null), d=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null); for(let i=0;i<rsiVals.length;i++){ if(i-period+1<0||rsiVals[i]==null) continue; let min=Infinity,max=-Infinity,ok=true; for(let j=i-period+1;j<=i;j++){const v=rsiVals[j]; if(v==null){ok=false; break;} if(v<min)min=v; if(v>max)max=v;} if(!ok)continue; sr[i]=(max===min)?0.5:(rsiVals[i]-min)/(max-min); const kv=sma(sr,kS,i); if(kv!=null)k[i]=kv*100; const dv=sma(k,dS,i); if(dv!=null)d[i]=dv; } return {k,d}; }

  }

}

function med(arr){ const a=arr.filter(v=>Number.isFinite(v)).sort((x,y)=>x-y); if(!a.length) return null; const m=Math.floor(a.length/2); return a.length%2?a[m]:(a[m-1]+a[m])/2; }
function pct(arr,p){ const a=arr.filter(v=>typeof v==='boolean'); if(!a.length) return null; return a.filter(Boolean).length/a.length; }

Use this command to fetch 90-day candles for HEI and SIREN directly from Bitunix into a local JSON file:

node - <<'NODE'
const fs = require("fs");

const BASE = "https://fapi.bitunix.com";
const SYMBOLS = ["HEIUSDT", "SIRENUSDT"];
const INTERVALS = { "15m":"15m", "1h":"1h", "4h":"4h", "12h":"12h", "1d":"1d" };
const LIMIT = 100;
const START = Date.now() - 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

async function fetchPage(symbol, interval, endTime) {
  const url = new URL("/api/v1/futures/market/kline", BASE);
  url.searchParams.set("symbol", symbol);
  url.searchParams.set("interval", interval);
  url.searchParams.set("limit", String(LIMIT));
  if (endTime != null) url.searchParams.set("endTime", String(endTime));
  const res = await fetch(url.toString(), { headers: { accept: "application/json" } });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(symbol + " " + interval + " HTTP " + res.status);
  const json = await res.json();
  return Array.isArray(json.data) ? json.data : [];
}

async function fetchAll(symbol, interval) {
  const dedup = new Map();
  let cursor;
  for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
    const rows = await fetchPage(symbol, interval, cursor);
    if (!rows.length) break;
    rows.sort((a,b) => Number(a.time) - Number(b.time));
    for (const r of rows) {
      const t = Number(r.time);
      if (!Number.isFinite(t)) continue;
      if (t < START) continue;
      dedup.set(t, {
        open: Number(r.open),
        high: Number(r.high),
        low: Number(r.low),
        close: Number(r.close),
        volume: Number(r.quoteVol ?? r.baseVol ?? 0),
        timestamp: t
      });
    }
    const oldest = Number(rows[0].time);
    if (!Number.isFinite(oldest) || oldest <= START) break;
    const next = oldest - 1;
    if (cursor != null && next >= cursor) break;
    cursor = next;
  }
  return Array.from(dedup.values()).sort((a,b) => a.timestamp - b.timestamp);
}

(async () => {
  const out = {};
  for (const symbol of SYMBOLS) {
    const base = symbol.replace(/USDT$/i, "");
    out[base] = {};
    for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(INTERVALS)) {
      const candles = await fetchAll(symbol, v);
      out[base][k] = candles;
      console.log(symbol, k, candles.length);
    }
  }
  fs.writeFileSync("apps/api/hl-candles-hei-siren-bitunix-90d.json", JSON.stringify(out));
  console.log("wrote apps/api/hl-candles-hei-siren-bitunix-90d.json");
})().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });

const fs=require('fs');

  const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8'));
  for(const [k,v] of Object.entries(d)) if(!merged[k]) merged[k]=v;
}

const TARGET=['SIREN','HEI','BEAT','ALLO'];
for(const s of TARGET){
  const rows=merged[s]?.['1d'];
  console.log(s,'1d candles',rows?rows.length:0);
}

function sma(arr, n, i){ if(i-n+1<0) return null; let s=0; for(let k=i-n+1;k<=i;k++) s+=arr[k]; return s/n; }
function rsi(closes, period=14){
  const out=Array(closes.length).fill(null);
  if(closes.length<=period) return out;
  let g=0,l=0;
  for(let i=1;i<=period;i++){ const d=closes[i]-closes[i-1]; if(d>=0)g+=d; else l-=d; }
  let ag=g/period, al=l/period;
  out[period]=al===0?100:100-(100/(1+ag/al));
  for(let i=period+1;i<closes.length;i++){
    const d=closes[i]-closes[i-1]; const gg=d>0?d:0, ll=d<0?-d:0;
    ag=(ag*(period-1)+gg)/period; al=(al*(period-1)+ll)/period;
    out[i]=al===0?100:100-(100/(1+ag/al));
  }
  return out;
}
function stochRsi(rsiVals, period=14, kS=3, dS=3){
  const sr=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null), k=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null), d=Array(rsiVals.length).fill(null);
  for(let i=0;i<rsiVals.length;i++){
    if(i-period+1<0||rsiVals[i]==null) continue;
    let min=Infinity,max=-Infinity,ok=true;
    for(let j=i-period+1;j<=i;j++){ const v=rsiVals[j]; if(v==null){ok=false;break;} if(v<min)min=v; if(v>max)max=v; }
    if(!ok) continue;
    sr[i]=(max===min)?0.5:(rsiVals[i]-min)/(max-min);
    const kv=sma(sr,kS,i); if(kv!=null) k[i]=kv*100;
    const dv=sma(k,dS,i); if(dv!=null) d[i]=dv;
  }
  return {k,d};
}
function findEvents(rows){
  const close=rows.map(r=>+r.close), vol=rows.map(r=>+r.volume);
  const ret=close.map((c,i)=> i? (c/close[i-1]-1)*100 : null);
  const e=[];
  for(let i=25;i<rows.length;i++){
    const r1=ret[i]??0, r2=((close[i]/close[i-2])-1)*100, r3=((close[i]/close[i-3])-1)*100;
    const vr=(sma(vol,7,i-1)||1)? vol[i]/(sma(vol,7,i-1)||1):null;
    if((r1>=18 || r2>=25 || r3>=30) && (vr==null || vr>=1.4)) e.push(i);
  }
  const uniq=[]; for(const i of e){ if(!uniq.length || i-uniq[uniq.length-1]>3) uniq.push(i); }
  return uniq;
}
function med(arr){ const a=arr.filter(v=>Number.isFinite(v)).sort((x,y)=>x-y); if(!a.length) return null; const m=Math.floor(a.length/2); return a.length%2?a[m]:(a[m-1]+a[m])/2; }

const all=[];
for(const sym of TARGET){
  const rows=merged[sym]?.['1d'];
  if(!rows||rows.length<40) continue;
  const close=rows.map(r=>+r.close), vol=rows.map(r=>+r.volume), high=rows.map(r=>+r.high), low=rows.map(r=>+r.low);
  const ret=close.map((c,i)=> i? (c/close[i-1]-1)*100 : null);
  const rr=rsi(close,14), s=stochRsi(rr,14,3,3);
  const events=findEvents(rows);
  console.log('\n===',sym,'events',events.length,'===');
  for(const i of events){
    const p=i-1;
    const v7=sma(vol,7,p), v14=sma(vol,14,p);
    let swingH=-Infinity,swingL=Infinity;
    for(let j=Math.max(0,p-20);j<=p;j++){ if(high[j]>swingH) swingH=high[j]; if(low[j]<swingL) swingL=low[j]; }
    const fibPos=(swingH-swingL)>0 ? (close[p]-swingL)/(swingH-swingL) : null;
    console.log(JSON.stringify({
      date:new Date(rows[i].timestamp).toISOString().slice(0,10),
      pumpDayReturnPct:+(ret[i]??0).toFixed(2),
      pre_rsi: rr[p]==null?null:+rr[p].toFixed(2),
      pre_stochK:s.k[p]==null?null:+s.k[p].toFixed(2),
      pre_stochD:s.d[p]==null?null:+s.d[p].toFixed(2),
      pre_stochCrossUp:(s.k[p]!=null&&s.d[p]!=null&&s.k[p]>s.d[p]&&s.k[p-1]!=null&&s.d[p-1]!=null&&s.k[p-1]<=s.d[p-1])||false,
      pre_volRatio7:v7?+(vol[p]/v7).toFixed(2):null,
      pre_volRatio14:v14?+(vol[p]/v14).toFixed(2):null,
      pre_fibPos20d:fibPos==null?null:+fibPos.toFixed(2)
    }));

    for(const lead of [1,2,3]){
      const q=i-lead; if(q<20) continue;
      const avgRange7=sma(high.map((h,idx)=>h-low[idx]),7,q);
      const avgRange20=sma(high.map((h,idx)=>h-low[idx]),20,q);
      let h=-Infinity,l=Infinity;
      for(let j=Math.max(0,q-20);j<=q;j++){ if(high[j]>h) h=high[j]; if(low[j]<l) l=low[j]; }
      all.push({

        rangeComp:(avgRange7&&avgRange20)?avgRange7/avgRange20:null,
        fibPos:(h-l)>0?(close[q]-l)/(h-l):null
      });
    }
  }
}

console.log('\n=== Aggregate across all available symbols/events ===');

function rsi(c,p=14){const o=Array(c.length).fill(null); if(c.length<=p)return o; let g=0,l=0; for(let i=1;i<=p;i++){const d=c[i]-c[i-1]; if(d>=0)g+=d; else l-=d;} let ag=g/p,al=l/p; o[p]=al===0?100:100-(100/(1+ag/al)); for(let i=p+1;i<c.length;i++){const d=c[i]-c[i-1],gg=d>0?d:0,ll=d<0?-d:0; ag=(ag*(p-1)+gg)/p; al=(al*(p-1)+ll)/p; o[i]=al===0?100:100-(100/(1+ag/al));} return o;}
function stoch(r,p=14,ks=3,ds=3){const sr=Array(r.length).fill(null),k=Array(r.length).fill(null),d=Array(r.length).fill(null);for(let i=0;i<r.length;i++){if(i-p+1<0||r[i]==null)continue;let mn=Infinity,mx=-Infinity,ok=true;for(let j=i-p+1;j<=i;j++){const v=r[j];if(v==null){ok=false;break;}if(v<mn)mn=v;if(v>mx)mx=v;}if(!ok)continue;sr[i]=(mx===mn)?0.5:(r[i]-mn)/(mx-mn);const kv=sma(sr,ks,i);if(kv!=null)k[i]=kv*100;const dv=sma(k,ds,i);if(dv!=null)d[i]=dv;}return{k,d};}

GitHub Copilot: Mostly yes, but not fully. I would call Gemini’s read directionally right, with 2 important corrections.

What it got right:
1. PREPARE SHORT is a staging signal, not an immediate market execution signal.
2. Macro RSI near 90 is strongly overbought context, which supports eventual mean-reversion risk.
3. 15m K at 100 while still above D means momentum has not cleanly rolled over yet.
4. Early timing plus low confidence means higher false-start risk.

What is likely wrong or overstated:
1. Arming 70% does not necessarily mean it must reach 100% to trigger.
In your engine, confidence-style thresholds are compared to configurable minimums, not a hard 100 completion model. See trade-engine.ts and trade-engine.ts.
2. Early does not always mean do not enter.
Your logic can still allow early entries when other gates pass, depending on signal class and reversal/EV filters. See trade-engine.ts and related reversal/EV checks around that section.
3. Confidence 27% is only a blocker if that specific confidence metric is a hard gate in that path.
For AI, you are still in shadow mode, so low AI confidence is logged but not blocking. See trade-engine.ts.

Bottom line:
Gemini’s qualitative market interpretation is good, but its execution logic assumption is too simplistic. Your bot does not run on a single “progress to 100%” trigger; it runs on multiple independent gates and thresholds.

import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';

const prisma = new PrismaClient();
const baseUrl = (process.env.BITUNIX_API_BASE_URL || 'https://fapi.bitunix.com').replace(//$/, '');

async function fetchActiveBitunixSymbols() {
  const u = new URL('/api/v1/futures/market/trading_pairs', baseUrl);
  const r = await fetch(u, { headers: { accept: 'application/json' } });
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`Bitunix HTTP ${r.status}`);
  const j = await r.json();
  const rows = Array.isArray(j?.data) ? j.data : [];
  const nonCrypto = new Set([
    'AAPL','AMZN','TSLA','GOOG','GOOGL','MSFT','NVDA','META','NFLX','COIN','MSTR','SPX','SP500','NDX','DJI','US30','NAS100','GER40','UK100','XAU','XAG','WTI','BRENT'
  ]);
  return new Set(
    rows
      .map((x) => ({ symbol: String(x?.symbol ?? '').toUpperCase().trim(), status: String(x?.symbolStatus ?? '').toUpperCase().trim() }))
      .filter((x) => x.symbol.endsWith('USDT') && x.status === 'OPEN')
      .map((x) => x.symbol.slice(0, -4))
      .filter((s) => s.length > 0 && !nonCrypto.has(s))
  );
}

async function main() {
  const active = await fetchActiveBitunixSymbols();
  if (active.size === 0) {
    throw new Error('No active Bitunix symbols fetched; aborting purge.');
  }

  const currentSymbols = await prisma.marketCandle.findMany({
    distinct: ['symbol'],
    select: { symbol: true }
  });
  const toDelete = currentSymbols
    .map((x) => x.symbol.toUpperCase())
    .filter((s) => !active.has(s));

  const beforeCandles = await prisma.marketCandle.count();
  const beforeTokens = await prisma.backfillToken.count();

  let deletedCandles = 0;
  let deletedTokens = 0;

  if (toDelete.length > 0) {
    const delC = await prisma.marketCandle.deleteMany({ where: { symbol: { in: toDelete } } });
    const delT = await prisma.backfillToken.deleteMany({ where: { symbol: { in: toDelete } } });
    deletedCandles = delC.count;
    deletedTokens = delT.count;
  }

  const afterCandles = await prisma.marketCandle.count();
  const afterTokens = await prisma.backfillToken.count();

  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    activeBitunixSymbols: active.size,
    symbolsInDb: currentSymbols.length,
    symbolsPurged: toDelete.length,
    deletedCandles,
    deletedBackfillTokens: deletedTokens,
    beforeCandles,
    afterCandles,
    beforeBackfillTokens: beforeTokens,
    afterBackfillTokens: afterTokens,
    purgeSample: toDelete.slice(0, 30)
  }, null, 2));
}

main()
  .catch((e) => {
    console.error(e instanceof Error ? e.stack ?? e.message : String(e));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  })
  .finally(async () => {
    await prisma.$disconnect();
  });
NODE

function pct(arr,p){ const a=arr.filter(v=>typeof v==='boolean'); if(!a.length) return null; return a.filter(Boolean).length/a.length; }

For a setup like PIPPIN, I’d use this order of importance:

1. All available weekly data to understand the full structure.
2. At least the last 12 to 18 months of daily data for the actual pattern.
3. More granular 4h and 1h data around the impulse, blow-off, and base.
4. The most recent 30 to 90 days on the execution timeframe, because that’s where the entry decision usually gets made.

The key point is that more data helps only if it is relevant. For pre-pump reads, the most useful history is:
- prior accumulation before the impulse
- the impulsive move itself
- the correction and base after the dump
- current compression and momentum behavior

So yes, all historical data is useful if you have it, but the real gain comes from having the full cycle context, not just a huge archive. If you want, I can give you a concrete checklist for what I’d want before I call something a legit pre-pump base versus just a dead bounce.

User: so here's my math and I know I'm wrong, but let's find a middle ground.  10x with 1% move is 10% gain. 3x a day = 30%. Do this successfully for 30 days we would have over 700K if success rate is in the 90% range. correct?

GitHub Copilot: Your raw compounding math is directionally right, but the assumptions are the part that breaks in real trading.

1. If you actually make +10% per trade and do 3 trades/day:
- Non-compounded day math: $30\%$ per day.
- Compounded per-trade day math: $(1.10)^3 - 1 = 33.1\%$ per day.

2. Starting from 300 USDT for 30 days:
- Using $30\%$ daily: $300 \times (1.30)^{30} \approx 785,000$.
- Using $33.1\%$ daily: $300 \times (1.331)^{30} \approx 1.6M$.

So yes, the arithmetic itself can print huge numbers.

Why it is not realistic:
1. A 1% adverse move at 10x is about -10% before fees/slippage/funding.
2. Win rate is not stable; regime changes crush high hit-rate systems.
3. Losses cluster (you can get streaks even with 90% win rate).
4. Execution friction (spread, slippage, missed fills, latency) compounds hard.
5. One oversized loss can erase many small wins.

Middle-ground framework (much safer for your 300 USDT):
1. Use 3x to 5x, not full-account 10x all-in.
2. Risk 0.75% to 1.25% of equity per trade.
3. Max 3 concurrent positions (as you said).
4. Daily hard stop at -3% equity, then no new entries.
5. Target 1% to 2% net daily average, not 30%.

That still compounds strongly without requiring near-perfect conditions.

User: what if we keep the 10x leverage, but reduce the TP to 5% which would .5% increase?

GitHub Copilot: That would make the system less aggressive and probably more robust.

At `10x` leverage:
1. `10%` ROE TP is about a `1.0%` underlying move.
2. `5%` ROE TP is about a `0.5%` underlying move.

As a liquidity-hunt trader, I think `10x` with `5%` TP is actually a cleaner fit if your goal is to grab quick dislocations and get out.

Why I like it more:
1. Liquidity hunts are often sharp but short-lived.
2. Expecting only `0.5%` underlying follow-through is more realistic than requiring a full `1%` every time.
3. Smaller target usually improves fill-to-exit completion and win rate.
4. It reduces the chance of watching a good scalp reverse before TP.

Tradeoff:
1. Lower average winner size.
2. Fees and slippage matter more.
3. You need the bot to stay disciplined and avoid overtrading, which we already tightened.

My opinion:
1. `10x / 5% TP` is more practical for this strategy than `10x / 10% TP`.

1. `300` is workable.

It’s there as a risk guardrail, not a bug.

In your engine, the session gate is explicitly designed to skip entries during a low-liquidity UTC window:
1. Defaults are set to 02:00 → 05:00 UTC in trade-engine.ts and trade-engine.ts.
2. The block check is implemented in trade-engine.ts.
3. When active, it hard-stops entry evaluation with reason `session block` and logs “low-liquidity UTC session” in trade-engine.ts.

Benefit:
1. Avoids thin-book hours where spreads/slippage and wick noise are usually worse.
2. Reduces false triggers and churn when market structure is less reliable.
3. Prevents paying high execution cost for lower-quality setups.

Cost:
1. You miss valid overnight moves.
2. Bot can appear “silent” even when signals exist.

If your priority is always-on alerting/trading, this guardrail is too restrictive for your use case and should be narrowed or disabled.

How to read it today:
1. In dashboard, those labels are just mapped from timing:
   - EARLY -> Prepare
   - MID -> Build
   - LATE or exhaustion conflict -> Caution  
   Source: dashboard.tsx
2. The bot’s actual “enter now” signal is READY, sent before execution candidates are acted on.  
   Source: trade-engine.ts
3. If live execution succeeds, you get OPENED, which is the real confirmation trade is in.  
   Source: telegram-service.ts
4. Timing is also hard-gated by config (default max is MID), so some candidates never execute even if they look interesting on screen.  
   Sources: trade-engine.ts, trade-engine.ts

So practically:
1. READY = eligible/green light.
2. OPENED = executed.
3. Prepare/Build = context progression only.

If you want, I can update wording so READY appears as “ENTER NOW” in Telegram and dashboard to remove ambiguity.

Because the dashboard is not rendering the full exchange universe directly. It only shows the current merged scanner snapshot from the API state, via dashboard.tsx and the WebSocket update in dashboard.tsx.

The important part is in the scanner service:
1. The background scanner rotates through a chunk of the universe each cycle instead of rescanning everything every time, in scan-service.ts and scan-service.ts.
2. The dashboard state is a merged cache of old rows plus fresh rows, in scan-service.ts.
3. A token disappears from that merged cache if it has not been refreshed within the snapshot TTL, or if it fails the active-symbol validation during merge, in scan-service.ts, scan-service.ts, and scan-service.ts.

For BTC specifically:
1. BTC is still in the perp universe. `/api/tokens?query=BTC` returns `BTC-PERP`.
2. BTC is not in the current `/api/state` results.
3. BTC is also not in the current cycle’s `skipped` list.

That means BTC is not being hidden by the dashboard UI. It is missing upstream from the live merged snapshot. In practice, that usually means one of two things:
1. BTC has not produced a retained fresh row recently enough, so it aged out of the merged cache.
2. BTC was not included in the currently retained merged set during chunk rotation, even though it still exists in the searchable universe.

So the short answer is: you are “losing tokens” because the dashboard is backed by a rotating, expiring snapshot, not a guaranteed always-full universe view.

If you want, I can patch this so majors like BTC/ETH/SOL are pinned every cycle or always shown in the dashboard even when their latest scan row is stale.

They are linked, but not the same thing.

With your current setup (LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true and SIM_SIGNAL_ONLY_MODE=false):
1. The bot sends a real exchange order (live trade).
2. It also creates an internal trade record for tracking, stats, dashboard, and lifecycle handling.
3. That internal record is marked as live, not pure simulation.

Code points:
1. Live mode switch is defined in trade-engine.ts.
2. On open, it executes live order first, then flags the trade as live and stores it in runtime state in trade-engine.ts.
3. On close, live-marked trades go through live close execution in trade-engine.ts.

If SIM_SIGNAL_ONLY_MODE=true, then it is simulation-only and no real order is sent.

import { PrismaClient, CandleInterval } from "@prisma/client";

type Candle = { ts:number; open:number; high:number; low:number; close:number; volume:number };

const prisma = new PrismaClient();
const TOKENS = ["H", "VELVET", "BEAT", "AIO", "ESPORTS"];

function rsi(values:number[], period=14): number[] {
  if (values.length < period + 1) return [];
  const out:number[] = [];
  let gain=0, loss=0;
  for (let i=1;i<=period;i++) {
    const d = values[i]-values[i-1];
    if (d>=0) gain += d; else loss -= d;
  }
  let avgGain = gain/period;
  let avgLoss = loss/period;
  out.push(avgLoss===0 ? 100 : 100-(100/(1+(avgGain/avgLoss))));
  for (let i=period+1;i<values.length;i++) {
    const d = values[i]-values[i-1];
    const g = d>0 ? d : 0;
    const l = d<0 ? -d : 0;
    avgGain = ((avgGain*(period-1))+g)/period;
    avgLoss = ((avgLoss*(period-1))+l)/period;
    out.push(avgLoss===0 ? 100 : 100-(100/(1+(avgGain/avgLoss))));
  }
  return out;
}

function stochRsi(rsiVals:number[], period=14, smoothK=3, smoothD=3) {
  if (rsiVals.length < period) return {k:[], d:[] as number[]};
  const stoch:number[] = [];
  for (let i=period-1;i<rsiVals.length;i++) {
    const w = rsiVals.slice(i-period+1, i+1);
    const lo = Math.min(...w);
    const hi = Math.max(...w);
    const v = hi===lo ? 0 : ((rsiVals[i]-lo)/(hi-lo))*100;
    stoch.push(v);
  }
  const k:number[] = [];
  for (let i=0;i<stoch.length;i++) {
    const s = stoch.slice(Math.max(0,i-smoothK+1), i+1);
    k.push(s.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/s.length);
  }
  const d:number[] = [];
  for (let i=0;i<k.length;i++) {
    const s = k.slice(Math.max(0,i-smoothD+1), i+1);
    d.push(s.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/s.length);
  }
  return {k,d};
}

function pct(a:number,b:number){ return a===0?0:((b-a)/a)*100; }

(async()=>{
  const now = Date.now();
  const fromH1 = new Date(now - 35*24*60*60*1000);

  const result:any[] = [];

  for (const symbol of TOKENS) {
    const h1Rows = await prisma.marketCandle.findMany({
      where:{ symbol, interval:CandleInterval.H1, timestamp:{ gte: fromH1 } },
      orderBy:{ timestamp:"asc" },
      select:{ timestamp:true, open:true, high:true, low:true, close:true, volume:true }
    });

    const d1Rows = await prisma.marketCandle.findMany({
      where:{ symbol, interval:CandleInterval.D1 },
      orderBy:{ timestamp:"asc" },
      select:{ timestamp:true, open:true, high:true, low:true, close:true, volume:true }
    });

    if (h1Rows.length < 60 || d1Rows.length < 30) {
      result.push({ symbol, error:"insufficient candle history", h1:h1Rows.length, d1:d1Rows.length });
      continue;
    }

    const h1:Candle[] = h1Rows.map(r=>({ts:new Date(r.timestamp).getTime(), open:Number(r.open), high:Number(r.high), low:Number(r.low), close:Number(r.close), volume:Number(r.volume)}));
    const d1:Candle[] = d1Rows.map(r=>({ts:new Date(r.timestamp).getTime(), open:Number(r.open), high:Number(r.high), low:Number(r.low), close:Number(r.close), volume:Number(r.volume)}));

    const latest = h1[h1.length-1];
    const c48 = h1.find(c=>c.ts >= latest.ts - 48*60*60*1000) ?? h1[0];
    const c24 = h1.find(c=>c.ts >= latest.ts - 24*60*60*1000) ?? h1[0];

    const vol24 = h1.filter(c=>c.ts > latest.ts - 24*60*60*1000).reduce((a,c)=>a+c.volume,0);
    const volPrev24 = h1.filter(c=>c.ts <= latest.ts - 24*60*60*1000 && c.ts > latest.ts - 48*60*60*1000).reduce((a,c)=>a+c.volume,0);

    const dRecent = d1.slice(-21);
    const dayVolumes = dRecent.map(c=>c.volume);
    const avgDailyVol20 = dayVolumes.slice(0,20).reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/Math.max(1,dayVolumes.slice(0,20).length);
    const latestDailyVol = dRecent[dRecent.length-1]?.volume ?? 0;
    const volDailyExpansion = avgDailyVol20>0 ? latestDailyVol/avgDailyVol20 : null;

    const dCloses = d1.map(c=>c.close);
    const dRsiSeries = rsi(dCloses,14);
    const dStoch = stochRsi(dRsiSeries,14,3,3);
    const dRsiNow = dRsiSeries[dRsiSeries.length-1] ?? null;
    const dRsiPrev = dRsiSeries[dRsiSeries.length-2] ?? null;
    const dK = dStoch.k[dStoch.k.length-1] ?? null;
    const dD = dStoch.d[dStoch.d.length-1] ?? null;
    const dKPrev = dStoch.k[dStoch.k.length-2] ?? null;
    const dDPrev = dStoch.d[dStoch.d.length-2] ?? null;

    const weekly:Candle[] = [];
    for (let i=0;i<d1.length;i+=7) {
      const chunk = d1.slice(i,i+7);
      if (!chunk.length) continue;
      weekly.push({
        ts: chunk[chunk.length-1].ts,
        open: chunk[0].open,
        high: Math.max(...chunk.map(x=>x.high)),
        low: Math.min(...chunk.map(x=>x.low)),
        close: chunk[chunk.length-1].close,
        volume: chunk.reduce((a,x)=>a+x.volume,0)
      });
    }

    const wCloses = weekly.map(c=>c.close);
    const wRsiSeries = rsi(wCloses,14);
    const wStoch = stochRsi(wRsiSeries,14,3,3);
    const wRsiNow = wRsiSeries[wRsiSeries.length-1] ?? null;
    const wK = wStoch.k[wStoch.k.length-1] ?? null;
    const wD = wStoch.d[wStoch.d.length-1] ?? null;

    const lookback20 = d1.slice(-20);
    const high20 = Math.max(...lookback20.map(c=>c.high));
    const low20 = Math.min(...lookback20.map(c=>c.low));
    const closeNow = d1[d1.length-1].close;
    const closePrev = d1[d1.length-2]?.close ?? closeNow;
    const nearHigh20 = high20>0 ? ((high20-closeNow)/high20)*100 : null;
    const rangePct20 = low20>0 ? ((high20-low20)/low20)*100 : null;

    const dailyCrossUp = (dKPrev!=null && dDPrev!=null && dK!=null && dD!=null) ? (dKPrev<=dDPrev && dK>dD) : false;
    const dailyOverheated = (dK!=null && dD!=null) ? (dK>88 && dD>85) : false;
    const dailyRsiRising = (dRsiNow!=null && dRsiPrev!=null) ? dRsiNow>dRsiPrev : false;

    let setup = "neutral";
    if (dailyCrossUp && !dailyOverheated && (wK==null || wK<80) && (vol24>volPrev24)) setup = "early-run candidate";
    else if (dailyOverheated && nearHigh20!=null && nearHigh20<3) setup = "late-run / risk of pullback";
    else if ((dK!=null && dD!=null && dK<dD && dK>70) || (vol24<volPrev24)) setup = "momentum cooling";

    result.push({
      symbol,
      priceMove: {
        pct24h: Number(pct(c24.close, latest.close).toFixed(2)),
        pct48h: Number(pct(c48.close, latest.close).toFixed(2))
      },
      volume: {
        vol24h: Number(vol24.toFixed(2)),
        volPrev24h: Number(volPrev24.toFixed(2)),
        vol24hVsPrev24h: volPrev24>0 ? Number((vol24/volPrev24).toFixed(2)) : null,
        latestDailyVolVs20dAvg: volDailyExpansion!=null ? Number(volDailyExpansion.toFixed(2)) : null
      },
      daily: {
        rsi14: dRsiNow!=null ? Number(dRsiNow.toFixed(2)) : null,
        stochRsiK: dK!=null ? Number(dK.toFixed(2)) : null,
        stochRsiD: dD!=null ? Number(dD.toFixed(2)) : null,
        crossUpNow: dailyCrossUp,
        overheated: dailyOverheated,
        rsiRising: dailyRsiRising
      },
      weekly: {
        rsi14: wRsiNow!=null ? Number(wRsiNow.toFixed(2)) : null,
        stochRsiK: wK!=null ? Number(wK.toFixed(2)) : null,
        stochRsiD: wD!=null ? Number(wD.toFixed(2)) : null
      },
      structure: {
        close: Number(closeNow.toFixed(8)),
        prevClose: Number(closePrev.toFixed(8)),
        high20: Number(high20.toFixed(8)),
        low20: Number(low20.toFixed(8)),
        distanceFrom20dHighPct: nearHigh20!=null ? Number(nearHigh20.toFixed(2)) : null,
        range20dPct: rangePct20!=null ? Number(rangePct20.toFixed(2)) : null
      },
      setup
    });
  }

  console.log(JSON.stringify({ asOf: new Date().toISOString(), tokens:TOKENS, analysis: result }, null, 2));
  await prisma.$disconnect();
})().catch(async (e)=>{ console.error(e); await prisma.$disconnect(); process.exit(1); });

import { PrismaClient, CandleInterval } from "@prisma/client";

type Candle = { ts:number; open:number; high:number; low:number; close:number; volume:number };
const prisma = new PrismaClient();

function rsi(values:number[], period=14): number[] {
  if (values.length < period + 1) return [];
  const out:number[] = [];
  let gain=0, loss=0;
  for (let i=1;i<=period;i++) {
    const d = values[i]-values[i-1];
    if (d>=0) gain += d; else loss -= d;
  }
  let avgGain = gain/period;
  let avgLoss = loss/period;
  out.push(avgLoss===0 ? 100 : 100-(100/(1+(avgGain/avgLoss))));
  for (let i=period+1;i<values.length;i++) {
    const d = values[i]-values[i-1];
    const g = d>0 ? d : 0;
    const l = d<0 ? -d : 0;
    avgGain = ((avgGain*(period-1))+g)/period;
    avgLoss = ((avgLoss*(period-1))+l)/period;
    out.push(avgLoss===0 ? 100 : 100-(100/(1+(avgGain/avgLoss))));
  }
  return out;
}

function stochRsi(rsiVals:number[], period=14, smoothK=3, smoothD=3) {
  if (rsiVals.length < period) return {k:[], d:[] as number[]};
  const stoch:number[] = [];
  for (let i=period-1;i<rsiVals.length;i++) {
    const w = rsiVals.slice(i-period+1, i+1);
    const lo = Math.min(...w);
    const hi = Math.max(...w);
    const v = hi===lo ? 0 : ((rsiVals[i]-lo)/(hi-lo))*100;
    stoch.push(v);
  }
  const k:number[] = [];
  for (let i=0;i<stoch.length;i++) {
    const s = stoch.slice(Math.max(0,i-smoothK+1), i+1);
    k.push(s.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/s.length);
  }
  const d:number[] = [];
  for (let i=0;i<k.length;i++) {
    const s = k.slice(Math.max(0,i-smoothD+1), i+1);
    d.push(s.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/s.length);
  }
  return {k,d};
}

function pct(a:number,b:number){ return a===0?0:((b-a)/a)*100; }

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

(async () => {
  const updates = [
    { key: "SCAN_ROTATION_CHUNK_SIZE", value: "30" },
    { key: "SCAN_LIMIT_TOKENS", value: "320" }
  ];

  for (const item of updates) {
    await prisma.runtimeSetting.upsert({
      where: { key: item.key },
      update: { value: item.value },
      create: { key: item.key, value: item.value }
    });
    console.log(`Updated ${item.key}=${item.value}`);
  }

  const verify = await prisma.runtimeSetting.findMany({
    where: { key: { in: updates.map(u => u.key) } },
    orderBy: { key: "asc" }
  });

More importantly, the settings haven't been picked up yet. Based on the copilot instructions, runtime settings are "loaded before app module usage"—meaning they're loaded at **startup**, not per-cycle. The service needs to be **restarted** to pick up the new DB values.

Perfect! I found the issue. In trade-engine.ts, `LIQUIDITY_HUNT_MIN_CONFIDENCE_PCT` is read from `process.env` at **startup** and stored in a constant—it's not re-read on each cycle. The service needs to be **restarted** to pick up the new DB values.

  const updates = [

    { key: "SCAN_LIMIT_TOKENS", value: "320" }
  ];

    await prisma.runtimeSetting.upsert({
      where: { key: item.key },
      update: { value: item.value },
      create: { key: item.key, value: item.value }

    where: { key: { in: updates.map(u => u.key) } },

  });

  await prisma.$disconnect();
})();

1. **Exchange rate limiting** (29 errors) — Bitunix hitting request limits; symbols get 2s backoff
2. **Candlestick gate still strict** (56 rejections) — Even with `requireDominance: false`, many still rejected
3. **Signal score floor** (58 rejections) — MIN_SCORE_THRESHOLD=3 still tight

The problem is **market conditions** + **cumulative gates**: each symbol must pass signal score + liquidity hunt + candlestick + HTF momentum + exchange capacity checks. Most are failing multiple gates simultaneously.

### Next Action Recommended

1. **Reduce entry barriers further** — Lower `SCORE_ENTRY_THRESHOLD` from 3 to 2
2. **Relax candlestick dominance entirely** — Set `ENTRY_CANDLE_CONFIRMATION_ENABLED = "false"` 
3. **Monitor if exchange throttling clears** — The 29 rate-limit rejections are preventing execution even on qualified candidates
